questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Always turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This lets you see your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if you see angry drivers around you?
questions.explanation: Stay safe from angry drivers by doing all of these: avoid eye contact, don't make gestures, and move away. Slow down or change lanes to put distance between you and them.

questions.question: Drinking and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you only have a few drinks.

questions.explanation: Drinking and driving is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol. It endangers you and everyone on the road.

questions.question: Road rage is:

options.text: An acceptable response to bad drivers.

questions.explanation: Road rage is a crime. If a small traffic problem turns into road rage, drivers can face legal punishment.

questions.question: When should drivers and passengers fasten their safety belts?
questions.explanation: Safety belts must be fastened by all passengers before you start the engine. This is the law and protects everyone in the car.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your chance of an accident.
Making you more aware of others.

questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, and sadness can hurt your driving. Stress makes it hard to concentrate on the road. Don't drive when you're emotionally upset.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to check for other cars. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate:

options.text: Go to the next exit and turn around there.
Ask the driver next to you for directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit and turn around there.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway. If you miss your exit, go to the next exit and safely turn around there.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: When turning left, you must give the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must give the right-of-way to oncoming traffic. You must also always give the right-of-way to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Any eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and look for pedestrians and cross traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce off fog and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says something else.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws even though there is construction.

questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from flaggers, signs, and police officers in construction zones. Not following them is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as well in the dark.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going downhill than smaller vehicles.
Need a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are larger and heavier, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: If you are driving while drowsy, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you cannot stay awake, get off the road and take a short nap. Drowsy driving is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal 3 to 5 seconds ahead. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a road with multiple lanes, move to the left lane before the intersection. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead shows red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead shows green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a traffic signal at the next intersection.

questions.question: You should use evasive steering action:

options.text: During normal driving when turning the wheel.
When avoiding a hazard while driving fast.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing up, signaling, turning on the radio, or using windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When avoiding a hazard while driving fast.
questions.explanation: At high speeds, even small steering movements move your vehicle a lot. If your brakes lock or your car slides, limit your steering to avoid moving into other lanes. Do not overcorrect, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
You can drive in the left lane.
You have the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. An obstacle, median, or barrier is ahead. You must stay on the right side of it.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Change lanes only when necessary. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What does the "E" in SIPDE mean?
questions.explanation: The "E" stands for "Execute a move." When facing danger, brake, speed up, turn, or make another move.

questions.question: In Louisiana, who must wear a safety belt?
questions.explanation: Louisiana law requires everyone in a vehicle to wear a safety belt. Safety belts save more lives than any other safety feature in cars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells drivers a traffic signal is coming. It is yellow with black markings. Be ready for red lights, yellow lights, and crossing traffic.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" happens when you:

options.text: Stare at the road for a long time.
Sleep too much the night before.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stare at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare ahead without looking around. You stop paying attention, and you may miss traffic slowing down or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: Traffic signs and road markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other cars are around.
Must be followed only when police are present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and road markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch which foot you use on the gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break. If you feel sleepy, pull over safely and nap, or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, use ____ to show you are turning.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals are broken, use hand signals to tell other drivers which way you are turning.
